new_statements.rule_in_words: The grammar treats Senhaja, like Northern Berber generally, as having no lexical (contrastive word-level) stress; prominence is regarded as a matter of sentence intonation and is not described. No placement rule is given.
new_statements.exceptions: None as such; one incidental footnote (p. 37) perceives stress on the u of a particular Zerqet plural form, showing the author hears word-level prominence but does not systematize it.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is framed as the received view for Northern Berber ('usually said'), adopted as the reason for omitting stress from this Senhaja grammar; prominence assigned to the phrase/intonation domain. Hedged and partly second-hand (cites Chaker 1995 on Berber generally), though it is the grammar author's own position for the language described.
new_statements.identity_note: Gutova 2021 is a polylectal grammar of all Senhaja de Srair varieties (Ketama, Taghzut, Hmed, Bunsar, Zerqet, Seddat, etc.), i.e. exactly glottocode senh1238; the stress sentence is stated for the language as a whole (and Northern Berber generally). Renisio 1932 covers Senhaja de Sraïr alongside Beni Iznassen and Rif (Tarifiyt) dialects.

sources.note: Ch. 2 intro, p. 83: 'Northern Berber languages are usually said to have no lexical stress'; stress 'rules' in Berber concern sentence intonation, which is left outside the study. No stress/accent subsection anywhere in the 792 pp; the phonology chapter treats consonants, vowels, schwa syllabification, semivowels, sandhi only. One incidental remark (fn. 35, p. 37) notes a Zerqet plural ṯiġwummriwin 'with the stress on u in the PL'. Ch. 12 lists Zwicky's 'accentual test' for clitics but does not apply a stress diagnostic to Senhaja.

sources.note: A brief grammatical sketch based on fieldwork in seven varieties, treating phonology and morphology with attention to Arabic contact. Tone is not mentioned in the abstract; Northern Berber is non-tonal and the author's 792-pp thesis never uses the word 'tone' and leaves intonation out of scope, so the phonology section most likely covers segments, schwa and sandhi only, at most repeating that there is no lexical stress. Unknown beyond the abstract.
